about.title: Soledad Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member unexpectedly is disorienting, and dealing with legal deadlines is often the last thing anyone wants to face. In Monterey County, corridors like Front Street, Monterey Street, Metz Road, and Gabilan Drive see regular traffic activity, and while Soledad's most recent final crash data reported no traffic fatalities, fatal incidents can still arise from vehicle collisions, workplace accidents, defective equipment, or negligent property conditions. California allows a spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring a wrongful death claim first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. We handle wrongful death claims for grieving families in Soledad. Our team can review what happened, explain the two-year filing deadline, and help determine who may have standing to pursue a claim. There's no cost for a consultation, and we only collect a fee if there's a recovery.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible under certain conditions. We can help sort out who in your family qualifies before decisions are made under pressure.

items.title: A Strict Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity was involved. We help protect your family's ability to file on time.

items.title: Losses Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance — not just medical bills. We can walk your family through what may apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Soledad?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a civil wrongful death claim. If a government agency, such as a county road department, may be involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim to be filed. Speaking with us soon after a loss helps make sure that window isn't missed.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim require a criminal case first?
items.answer: No — a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges that may or may not be filed. Even if no criminal case is pursued, or if one results in an acquittal, families can still bring a civil claim for damages. The two proceedings follow different rules and different burdens of proof.

items.question: My family member died in a crash near Metz Road — does that change anything?
items.answer: Location itself doesn't determine whether a claim exists, but it can affect what records are available, such as collision reports or witness statements tied to that stretch of road. Our team is familiar with Monterey County matters and can help gather what's needed regardless of exactly where in Soledad the incident happened.
